items.summary: It’s becoming a disturbing trend for the Canucks. Vancouver has been outscored 11-0 in the final periods of the past five games, including Tuesday’s setback to Carolina. It’s simply not a recipe to win games.
items.body: VANCOUVER – Nic Deslauriers has hurt a lot of opponents in the National Hockey League. Just not often with his stick. The 35-year-old heavyweight scored twice Tuesday, matching his goal total from the last two years, as the Carolina Hurricanes pulled away from the Vancouver Canucks in the third period to win 6-3 at Rogers Arena. Just like the Tampa Bay Lightning pulled away in the third period against the Canucks on Sunday. Like the Florida Panthers did the game before that. Like both the New York Rangers and Islanders did last week. The Canucks have lost eight consecutive games (0-7-1), but in these last five have been tied three times after 40 minutes, trailed by a goal once, and led by two in another. But Vancouver has been outscored 11-0 in the final periods of these last games and lost them all. Several of these teams, like the reigning Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes, are also NHL heavyweights. And when they come out swinging in the bell round, the Canucks have been pushed back to the ropes and tried to survive by covering up. “It’s super frustrating,” longest-tenured Canuck Brock Boeser said. “I mean, you never want to lose this many games in a row in this league. I know we're in a kind of rebuilding stage, but it doesn't matter; it sucks to lose. With a goal in the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s 6-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday, Kucherov has tied Stamkos as the highest scoring player in Lightning franchise history with 1,137 points. The goal came on a breakaway just over five minutes into the third period, when Kucherov poked the puck away from Vegas defenseman Jeremy Lauzon at the Tampa Bay blueline, exhibited some of his trademark deceptive stick handling, and beat goaltender Carter Hart clean to the blocker side for the Lightning’s sixth and final goal of the game. In nine games this season, Kucherov has four goals and nine assists for a team-leading 13 points . Last season, the Russian national notched 44 goals and 86 assists for 130 points in 76 games en route to winning the Hart Trophy as league MVP. Selected by Tampa Bay in the second round of the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, Kucherov had a modest rookie season in 2013-14, putting up just nine goals and nine assists for 18 points in 52 games. Over the next couple of seasons, Kucherov established himself as a high quality top six forward, playing on the Lightning’s “triplets line” along with Tyler Johnson and Ondrej Palat. In the 2016-17 season, Kucherov ascended into being one the game’s truly elite offensive threats, and hasn’t looked back since. items.body: COLUMBUS — They rained jeers down on Kirill Marchenko when his name was first announced through the Nationwide Arena loudspeakers. They volleyed even more when he first stepped onto the ice. More still the first time he touched the puck, and every time after that, too. But the crowd filling the Columbus Blue Jackets’ arena booed loudest eight minutes into this tense Tuesday night affair, when their former starring man darted to the net, turned his skate blades toward the crease, and let an Auston Matthews bullet pass careen off his foot and into the back of the cage, spurring the beginning of an eventual 6-2 Toronto Maple Leafs rout. “You know, the best thing is to score early, I think, so he got that one right away,” head coach Jim Hiller said after the dust settled on his club’s impressive road win. “That was probably a pretty good relief for him. And I thought he played well. He was dangerous. He was what the Columbus fans have come to see out of him — a dangerous player, and pretty electric.” There was no love lost between Marchenko and the city he called home for the past four years. items.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid sets NHL record for assists through first nine games
items.summary: As the Edmonton Oilers held off the Minnesota Wild for a 4-3 overtime win on home ice, McDavid dished out a trio of assists, including his 20th helper of the year on Evan Bouchard’s game-winning goal.
items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid start to the 2026-27 season hit a new level on Tuesday night. As the Edmonton Oilers held off the Minnesota Wild for a 4-3 overtime win on home ice, McDavid dished out a trio of assists, including his 20th helper of the year on Evan Bouchard's game-winning goal. It set the NHL record for most assists through the first nine games of a season, per Sportsnet Stats. Already a three-time Hart Trophy winner, McDavid appears to have his eyes set on a fourth early into his 12th campaign. McDavid now has an NHL-leading 26 points and has helped the Oilers break out to a 7-1-1 record as they look to bounce back from a disappointing first-round exit in the Stanley Cup Playoffs last spring. That blistering start puts the 29-year-old on pace for 242 points over 84 games, which would shatter the NHL record of 215 set by Wayne Gretzky in the 1985-86 season. McDavid's previous career high came in 2022-23, when he scored 64 goals and dished out 89 assists for 153 points. Numbers that seem to have a small chance of standing up beyond this season, so long as the superstar centre can keep producing at this historic pace.

items.title: Oilers’ Nugent-Hopkins to return Thursday vs. Hurricanes
items.body: Already off to a red-hot start this season, the Edmonton Oilers are getting a major piece back from injury. Forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins will be back in the Oilers' lineup Thursday when they host the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, head coach Mike Babcock told reporters after Tuesday's win over the Minnesota Wild. Nugent-Hopkins has yet to lace up this season after suffering a lower-body injury in practice ahead of the team's season opener in late September. He was placed on the injured reserve soon after on Oct. 1. The 33-year-old is entering his 16th season with the Oilers after being selected by the team first overall at the 2011 NHL draft. The forward from Burnaby, B.C., had 20 goals last year — hitting that mark for the seventh time in his career — while adding 36 assists over 72 games. He has 804 points (291 goals, 513 assists) over 1,031 regular-season games with Edmonton. Nugent-Hopkins is expected to centre Edmonton's second line this season. The Oilers are 7-1-1 to start the season and sit second in the Pacific behind the Vegas Golden Knights.

items.summary: This 4-3 overtime loss for the Montreal Canadiens was the result of a series of bad decisions, and the last one will haunt the player who needed a win most.
items.body: MONTREAL — This 4-3 overtime loss for the Montreal Canadiens was the result of a series of bad decisions, and the last one will haunt the player who needed a win most. Goaltender Jakub Dobes came into the game at 1-2-1, down on his luck and with his confidence spiralling. The opportunity to change that was right in his hands before he fumbled it away with a penalty in overtime. To see Dobes drop it as he did was to know this might get worse for him before it gets better. Just 20 seconds after the struggling goaltender needlessly interfered with Collin Graf, Macklin Celebrini wired home the overtime winner with his second goal of Tuesday's game. We don’t know what Dobes was trying to do in that instant, because he wasn’t available to explain it after the game. But we know that, like with everything else he does, he was trying his hardest — the quality that endeared him most to his teammates through his extremely successful rookie season, but also the quality that is plaguing him most right now. It started off with a great win in Toronto, in which Dobes made the difference. But then he allowed six goals in a loss to Pittsburgh. Then five goals in a loss to Carolina. Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid had three assists for the Oilers (7-1-1), who have won two in a row and seven of their last eight. Mathieu Joseph also scored. Devon Levi made 27 stops to earn the win in the Oilers’ net. Joel Eriksson Ek, Kirill Kaprizov and Ryan Hartman replied for the Wild (6-2-2), who saw a two-game winning streak halted. Wild: Kaprizov picked up an assist and his league-leading 11 th goal to hit 17 points on the season, the second-most through 10 games in franchise history behind his own 21 in 2024-25. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points streak to all nine games. The Oilers' captain became just the sixth player in NHL history with 25 points before their 10th game in a season. Also achieving the feat —Mario Lemieux (three times, most 33), Mike Bossy (28), Wayne Gretzky (twice; most 27), Brent Sutter (25) and Marcel Dionne (25). With 26 points, McDavid was already more than a quarter of the way to his 10th career 100-point season. With the Wild serving a too-many-men penalty, Bouchard scored his seventh of the season on a bomb of a shot with 1:28 remaining in overtime. He scored the winner on his 27th birthday. Both teams rely heavily on their top lines. The Oilers came into the game with 19 goals from their top trio, while the rest of the team scored 18. items.body: PHILADELPHIA -- Trevor Zegras has always had a vibe to him, a skating version of yacht rock in the crash-bang heavy metal clamor of an NHL game. The Philadelphia Flyers forward has been described by close friends and coaches as an energetic golden retriever and Jeff Spicoli, Sean Penn's character in the 1980s film "Fast Times at Ridgemont High." "He's just go-with-the-flow kind of guy, surfer vibe," Flyers teammate Denver Barkey said. "Nothing really bothers him." But when Zegras signed a four-year, $36.5 million contract ($9.125 million average annual value) with the Flyers on July 15, general manager Daniel Briere said it was time for the 25-year-old forward to emerge as a leader. Zegras will never be compared to the likes of "Captain Serious" Jonathan Toews , but in his seventh NHL season, he understands his place in the League and importance in a Flyers dressing room that began the season with five players age 22 and younger. Philadelphia had six rookies in the lineup for its 3-2 win against the Colorado Avalanche on Monday. "There's just a point in time where you realize I'm an older guy and leader, but they're definitely young and they ask a lot of questions," Zegras said. "I feel like there are some things I can relate to, being in their shoes not that long ago. They're good dudes and good people and that makes it easy." One of the ways Zegras has chosen to make it easy on his younger teammates is opening his Philadelphia-area townhouse to them. That began last season with Barkey, who was recalled from Lehigh Valley of the American Hockey League in December 2025. items.body: Former Milwaukee batboy plans to be on hand for team’s return after 44 years The 2026-27 NHL schedule, and maybe fate, has the Florida Panthers in Chicago for off days on Friday and Saturday, putting general manager Bill Zito about a 90-minute drive or a brief flight away from where the Milwaukee Brewers will host the Tampa Bay Rays for the first two games of the World Series. Zito, who grew up about 15 minutes north of Milwaukee in Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin, plans to take advantage of the mini break before the Panthers play the Blackhawks on Sunday to get to American Family Field to watch the Brewers’ first World Series appearance in 44 years. “Yeah, I'm trying to get tickets,” Zito said Tuesday. “So, we'll absolutely get going.” Zito had an inside view the last time the Brewers were in the World Series in 1982. Now 62, Zito at the time was a batboy and clubhouse attendant for the Brewers from 1981-83. Zito raced home with his son, Billy, following the Panthers’ 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks last Thursday in time to see the final outs of the Brewers’ pennant-clinching 6-4 victory against the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series. The excitement brought Zito back to watching the Brewers advance to the World Series by defeating the California Angels for the American League pennant in 1982. “It's an appreciation of, obviously, how fortunate and lucky I was to be able to have that full experience in the first place, and the World Series for Milwaukee and for friends,” Zito said. “… My dad's still in Milwaukee. items.title: Mikko Rantanen completes hat trick in overtime, Stars beat Bruins
items.body: DALLAS — Mikko Rantanen scored in overtime to complete a hat trick, and the Dallas Stars beat Boston 3-2 on Tuesday night to snap the Bruins' five-game winning streak. It was the 11th career three-goal game for Rantanen and his first in the regular season since joining the Stars in a trade during the 2024-25 season. He became the fourth Stars player with an overtime hat trick since the team moved to Dallas for the 1993-94 season. Rantanen got his first goal early in the second period to tie the game at 1-1, and he tied it again in the third. His winner came on the power play at 3:52 of overtime when he did some nifty stick work in close and fired a shot past the left shoulder of Jeremy Swayman, who earlier in the extra period stopped Wyatt Johnston on two breakaway attempts 10 seconds apart and finished with 22 saves. Jake Oettinger stopped 18 shots for Dallas (5-3-1) in its third straight win. Matthew Poitras and James Hagens scored for the Bruins (7-2-1), who concluded their Western Conference trip at 3-0-1. Boston went 0 for 4 on the power play against Dallas, which came in allowing an NHL-best 1.5 goals per game and had the fourth-best penalty kill in the league. The Stars have allowed one power-play goal on opponents' last 25 chances. Roope Hintz had a shot from in close deflect off the leg of Boston’s Charlie McAvoy, and the loose puck ricocheted directly to Rantanen, who poked it past Swayman with 6:22 left in regulation to tie it at 2-all.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google The Washington Capitals got quite the fright when number-one goaltender Logan Thompson appeared to tweak something early in the second period on Tuesday night against the Los Angeles Kings . Thompson made a point-blank save on Kings star winger Artemi Panarin , but was very slow to get up. He continued to flex and stretch out his left leg throughout the rest of the game. Thompson was able to finish the night in net, a 5-2 defeat to the Kings, making 21 total saves on the 25 shots he faced. After the game, RMNB’s Katie Adler asked Capitals head coach Spencer Carbery whether the team had any lingering injury concerns about Thompson. “Not as of now,” Carbery said. “I’ll talk to Serbs (head athletic trainer Jason Serbus), but nothing right now.” With the loss, Thompson is now 4-3-0, with a 2.90 goals-against average and a .901 save percentage. According to MoneyPuck , he allowed 1.3 more goals than expected against the Kings, bringing his 2026-27 total down to 4.2 goals saved above expected. The Capitals don’t play again until they host the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday night. They are scheduled for three straight days of practice at MedStar Capitals Iceplex until then. items.summary: Auston Matthews had a goal and an assist in his 700th NHL game and the Toronto Maple Leafs scored four straight goals in the second period to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 6-2 on Tuesday for their second road victory of the season.
items.body: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Auston Matthews had a goal and an assist in his 700th NHL game and the Toronto Maple Leafs scored four straight goals in the second period to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 6-2 on Tuesday for their second road victory of the season. Easton Cowan and Jack Roslovic each had a goal and two assists, William Nylander had a goal and an assist, and Morgan Rielly added three assists. Kirill Marchenko and Marshall Rifai also scored, and Anthony Stolarz stopped 33 shots for the Maple Leafs. Jake Christiansen and Charlie Coyle scored for the Blue Jackets. They have been outscored 15-3 in the second period through eight games and lost for the fourth time in five games. Jet Greaves stopped 14 shots before being pulled in the second period after allowing his fifth goal. Cam Talbot stopped two of the three shots he faced in relief. Christiansen’s first goal of the season at 2:38 of the first period gave Columbus the early lead. Marchenko, who faced unrelenting boos in his first visit since being traded by Columbus, pulled Toronto even with a power-play goal at 8:16. Kent Johnson appeared to put Columbus ahead with a one-timer, but the goal was waved off because time had expired. The second period was all Toronto, starting with goals 46 seconds apart from Nylander and Matthews, who has 16 goals and 27 points in 21 career games against the Blue Jackets. Colton Sissons’ assist on Nylander's goal extended his points streak to four games. Cowan’s short-handed goal gave the Maple Leafs a three-goal lead at 6:48 before Roslovic made it 5-1 and chased Greaves from the net at 12:03. Coyle scored his first goal of the season off the backhand at 4:13 of the third period to make it 5-2 before Rifai extended Toronto's lead with 3:02 to go.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images The Dylan Larkin saga continues in Hockeytown, though the former captain is trying to give himself the best opportunity to be shipped out of town. According to Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press , the Detroit Red Wings center has expanded his list of potential trade destinations to 10 teams. Larkin made headlines back in June, as the Washington Township, Mich. native asked to be traded from his hometown team . Originally, the list of teams he’d be willing to go to was just the Florida Panthers , Minnesota Wild , and Vegas Golden Knights . After then-general manager Steve Yzerman wasn’t able to finalize a deal to his liking, Larkin tried to better his chances by adding the Dallas Stars to his list. However, that didn’t seem to work. Even after Yzerman stepped down as GM, Larkin still wanted out of Detroit. In September, it was reported that Larkin expressed interest in being sent to the Colorado Avalanche , Tampa Bay Lightning , or Washington Capitals . Yet, in the past few weeks, nothing has changed, with Larkin having to play games for the Wings to keep his trade value intact. Now, according to St. James, Larkin would be willing to be traded to the Carolina Hurricanes , New Jersey Devils or even the upstart Utah Mammoth . He has the ability to determine his future home, as Larkin has a full no-trade clause on his current contract, which carries an AAV of $8.7 million through the 2030-31 campaign. items.body: WASHINGTON — Adrian Kempe scored twice and the Los Angeles Kings got their first win of the season, rallying from an early deficit to beat the Washington Capitals 5-2 on Tuesday night. Artemi Panarin, Erik Gustafsson and Scott Laughton also scored for Los Angeles (1-4-2), and former Capitals goalie Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves. Ryan Leonard and Cole Hutson scored for the Capitals, who took a 2-0 lead in the first period but were held scoreless for the final 41:25. Washington's Logan Thompson stopped 21 shots. The Kings, who came in having scored just four goals over their previous four games and 12 goals through six games, lost second-line center Quinton Byfield to an upper-body injury in the first period. He played just 2:44. Hutson put the Capitals ahead 2-0 on the power play with 1:25 left in the first, but Kempe found the net less than a minute later and Panarin scored 2 seconds before the intermission. Gustafsson put the Kings ahead at 7:28 of the third on the power play. Kempe scored his second goal midway through the third, and Laughton added an empty-netter that gave the Kings their highest-scoring game of the season. Absent the injured Pierre Luc-Dubois and Justin Sourdif down the middle of their forward ranks, the Capitals were unable to beat Kuemper, who played for Washington from 2022-24.

items.body: Dylan Larkin has reportedly opened up his trade request to include more teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reports that Larkin's trade list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. The now-former captain of the Red Wings requested a trade in the spring and St. James reported at the time that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, once he was removed from his post on July 15, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations. That search is ongoing but Shawn Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. St. James reports one of the reasons a trade has not happened yet is that the Red Wings continue to ask for "value-now" players instead of a package of prospects and draft picks. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. Larkin has one goal and three points in six games for the Red Wings this season after missing training camp with an upper-body injury.

items.body: OTTAWA — Brady Tkachuk ’s finest moment as an Ottawa Senator may have doubled as his final great one with the club. It was in the immediate aftermath of a Game 4, overtime win against the Toronto Maple Leafs in the first round of the 2025 Stanley Cup Playoffs. items.title: Why haven’t the Ducks, Sharks taken the next step?

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It has been a disappointing start to the year for the NHL’s three Californian teams. The Los Angeles Kings are the last winless team in the league, and both the Anaheim Ducks and San Jose Sharks sit at NHL .500 and comfortably back of the pace in the Pacific Division. While the Kings have an aging roster and are entrenched in a downward trend, both the Ducks and Sharks have young, talented cores and entered the year with high expectations. While the Ducks were handicapped by the offer sheet to Leo Carlsson, they were still a playoff team a year ago, and the standard was to repeat that performance at least. Meanwhile in the Bay Area, the hype around this young core led by Macklin Celebrini has reached a fever pitch, and general manager Mike Grier added plenty of veterans to a group that pushed for a playoff spot last year. On Tuesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , host former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton was joined by former NHL video coach Steve Peters to discuss the disappointing starts to the year for the two young, promising teams out of California. Carter Hutton : Right now we’re watching two young teams that we thought were going to come out flying, the Sharks and the Ducks, and these are teams that I’ve been kind of watching… the Sharks don’t have a regulation win, Petey, and the Ducks have dropped their last three being outscored 13-6. What are your concerns about these younger teams who were supposed to take the step forward in the Pacific Division? Steve Peters : Well this is hard, because when you look at the Pacific Division, the top two teams are the top two teams now. It’s Vegas and Edmonton. items.summary: While the Blue Jackets’ side of the trade brought an end to a prolonged dispute that seemed all but certain to end in a move for Kirill Marchenko, for Matthew Knies, the news hit like a crosscheck to the gut.
items.body: COLUMBUS — It’s been three weeks since the blockbuster trade that shook up the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ locker room on the eve of the 2026-27 campaign. Three weeks since Matthew Knies got word, one night before Toronto's season-opener, that he’d been dealt to Columbus, bringing an end to a three-year run that saw the 24-year-old emerge briefly as a core piece in blue and white. Nearly a month on, with seven games in a Blue Jackets sweater under his belt, Knies is still adjusting to life in Ohio after the abrupt change of address. “Last night was my first night out of the hotel in Columbus,” the winger said Tuesday, ahead of his first meeting with his former club. “It feels like I’ve been on the road for quite a while now. You know, first home-cooked meal in a while — you don’t really think about that kind of stuff when you get traded, just how long it takes to get all of your belongings and stuff over here, getting my parents situated to be able to come watch the games, and family and friends. It’s different.” Capping off a summer that saw the Maple Leafs revamp seemingly all corners of the organization, general manager John Chayka's biggest swing was no doubt the seven-piece deal that sent Knies to the Blue Jackets and brought Kirill Marchenko back to Toronto, ending a months-long spell in the rumour mill for both wingers. Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman confirmed that Duehr successfully cleared waivers. Oct. 19th: According to Mike McIntyre of the Winnipeg Free Press , the Winnipeg Jets have placed forward Walker Duehr on waivers. Duehr began the season on the Jets’ season-opening injured reserve due to a preseason lower-body injury. Duehr, 28, is about to begin his second season with the Jets organization. He signed a one-year, $775K contract with Winnipeg ahead of the 2025-26 season. He spent much of the year with the AHL’s Manitoba Moose, scoring 17 goals and 34 points in 62 games with a +4 rating. The Jets recalled Duehr for a three-game stretch in early March, and he went scoreless while averaging 9:30 of ice time per game. Despite limited exposure in the NHL last season, Winnipeg quickly extended Duehr for added depth moving forward. One day after the Carolina Hurricanes lifted the Stanley Cup, the Jets signed Duehr to a two-year, $1.75MM ($875K AAV) contract through the 2027-28 campaign. Although he hasn’t gotten many chances with the Jets, Duehr gained NHL experience earlier in his professional career. A tertiary scorer at Minnesota State University-Mankato, Duehr signed as a collegiate free agent with the Calgary Flames toward the end of the 2020-21 campaign. Duehr played 84 games with the Flames from 2021 to 2025, scoring nine goals and 19 points with a -9 rating, averaging 8:55 of ice time per game. Despite the limited offensive totals, Duehr also registered 150 hits in that span, showing what he can contribute in the bottom six.

items.body: Forward played eight seasons in Canada’s capital, was team captain before trade to Atlantic rival OTTAWA -- Members of the Ottawa Senators will meet up with Brady Tkachuk for dinner on Tuesday, and there will be no hard feelings. Instead, it will be an opportunity to catch up while the Florida Panthers are in town. There will be understanding and a reunion with an old friend. We’re still going to be friends. And every player in the League is open to doing what they want.” Tkachuk, the former Senators captain, will return here on a hot streak. items.body: Festivities for the outdoor game in Winnipeg on Sunday will begin at noon local with the Scotiabank FanFest at the University of Manitoba's U Lot. items.summary: Through his first 10 games, Gavin McKenna has flashed the electrifying skill set that made him a consensus first overall selection while navigating the structural and defensive growing pains typical of an 18-year-old rookie. Here is how his start compares to other forwards selected with the top pick in past years.
items.body: When the Toronto Maple Leafs selected Gavin McKenna first overall, it was hard not to have high hopes given he was joining a team already flush with high-end forward talent. For a moment, there was debate whether the Leafs were better served going in another direction with the pick, whether it was Ivar Stenberg, who was viewed as a more two-way winger, or even a defenceman, which was high up on the team's list of needs. Instead of focusing on need, Toronto went with the player projected to have the higher ceiling given the scoring ability McKenna showed in the WHL and NCAA. The Leafs also did their due diligence when they met with McKenna to see how the 18-year-old forward would handle the spotlight of playing in Toronto. Ten games into his professional career, it's easy to just look at the box score and make an evaluation of McKenna's play. However, in order to paint a better picture, other factors have to be considered. To understand the trajectory of McKenna's start, here's a comparison to other forwards who were selected first overall since 2007. McKenna's six points put him in the middle of the group of first overall selections examined in this comparison. items.body: Register Login Kings Activate Mats Zuccarello By Brennan McClain | at October 20, 2026 1:00 pm The winless Los Angeles Kings are getting a key reinforcement back to their forward corps. According to a team announcement , the Kings have activated winger Mats Zuccarello from the injured reserve. Los Angeles had two openings on their 23-man roster, so no corresponding transaction was necessary. Simply put, the Kings need all the help they can get. After the Philadelphia Flyers defeated the Ottawa Senators this past Saturday, the Los Angeles Kings remained the only team yet to win their first game of the 2026-27 season. The Kings are dead last in the NHL three weeks into the season. There are two main reasons for that. First, Los Angeles has gotten dismal play from between the pipes, with the tandem of Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg managing an .861 SV%. Hardly conducive to winning. Secondly, the Kings struggle to score, which has been a problem for a while. Last season, despite making the postseason for the fifth consecutive year, Los Angeles finished 29th in scoring. This season, albeit early, the Kings are 31st in scoring, just ahead of the Flyers. Fortunately, with Zuccarello returning, this should improve. He’s been limited to one assist in two games this season due to an undisclosed injury. However, even on the wrong side of 30, Zuccarello is one year removed from scoring 15 goals and 54 points in 59 games with the Minnesota Wild. It will take more than Zuccarello to turn things around, but there is a silver lining for the Kings. They have played the fewest games in the league so far, so there is still time to recover.

items.summary: Through their first 10 percent of the 2026-27 campaign, the Boston Bruins s have been one of the NHL's most dangerous teams. But can their strong start last?
items.body: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Eric Canha-Imagn Images Can The Boston Bruins Shock The Rest Of The NHL's Atlantic Division? Adam Proteau Partner Oct 20, 2026 5:12 PM Published Oct 20, 2026 5:12 PM Through their first 10 percent of the 2026-27 campaign, the Boston Bruins s have been one of the NHL's most dangerous teams. But can their strong start last? After the Boston Bruins had a solid 2025-26 season, some observers – this one included – wondered whether they could replicate it, let alone improve on it. But in their first nine games, the Bruins have a 7-2-0 record, good enough for first place in the Atlantic Division and second place in the Eastern Conference. The good news doesn't stop there for Boston. They've won five straight games, and their plus-15 goal differential is the second-best in the entire NHL. Meanwhile, goalie Jeremy Swayman has a stellar .934 save percentage and 1.85 GAA, making him an early front-runner for the Vezina Trophy as the league's best netminder. More Videos Their overall depth has really shined as well, with a whopping 11 players who've generated at least five points. Boston's terrific start is another indication that the Atlantic is going to be one of the NHL's most competitive divisions, and Bruins fans have to be extremely pleased with head coach Marco Sturm, who is making a great case for the Jack Adams Award as the league's best bench boss. That said, it's still reasonable to be skeptical of the Bruins and where they rank among legitimate Stanley Cup threats. They are still very much a team transitioning from the Brad Marchand/Patrice Bergeron era, and have 12 players who are 27 or younger, and six players who are 30 years old or older. The Bruins of today are going to look significantly different than the Bruins team a year or two from now

items.summary: Roy suffered a lower-body injury earlier this month, leading to him being placed on injured reserve.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A veteran presence is set to return to action. The Washington Capitals have activated defenseman Matt Roy off injured reserve, with head coach Spencer Carbery announcing that he’ll be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Capitals play host to the Los Angeles Kings . Roy has missed the past six games due to a lower-body injury that he suffered back on Oct. 3 against the Tampa Bay Lightning . The Capitals have been solid during that time, going 4-2-0, winning each of their past two games, including a 4-2 victory over the New Jersey Devils this past Saturday. Roy was placed on injured reserve a little over a week later to make room for fellow blueliner Justin Holl. Roy’s injury came in the second game of the 2026-27 campaign. He was in the lineup for the season opener on Friday night, when Washington came away with a 5-2 win over the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . Roy played 22:29 in the victory, but didn’t put his name on the scoresheet. The 31-year-old is in his third season in the U.S. capital. After five seasons with the Kings, the Detroit native signed with the Capitals as a free agent, inking a six-year, $34.5 million contract with the team in July 2024. After five consecutive seasons with at least 20 points , Roy’s production took a dip last season on a Washington team that struggled, posting just two goals and 19 points in 79 games. In 518 regular-season games in the NHL, Roy has notched 29 goals and 120 assists for 149 points, with another eight points in 28 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Accountability is a big thing in the NHL and it must be maintained. But teenagers like Gavin McKenna with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Alberts Smits with the New York Rangers and Ivar Stenberg with the San Jose Sharks are your future, and that's where handing out minutes becomes a balancing act for a coach. You're feeling the pressure to win now, especially in big markets like Toronto and New York. But you're working with players who are vitally important to the future of the team, both later this season and long beyond it, and who are probably making mistakes in the details of the game. items.summary: Brady Tkachuk isn’t ready to let his Ottawa Senators jerseys go to waste.
items.body: Brady Tkachuk isn't ready to let his Ottawa Senators jerseys go to waste. The Florida Panthers forward plans to donate any sweaters tossed on the ice during his return game to Ottawa on Wednesday to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa, he said on an episode of his podcast released Tuesday. Tkachuk was granted a trade request to team up with brother Matthew in Florida over the off-season, spurning the Senators despite his captaincy. His first game back promises to bring some fireworks, with Tkachuk likely to hear raucous boos from the Senators faithful. "I think, once we get there, it’s going to hit a little more," Tkachuk said Monday. "Now it still feels like that game you circle on the calendar, and I bet for a lot of people, can’t believe it’s here, but once we land in Ottawa, set foot and see some of the guys, it’ll be, ‘All right, it’s here.' It’s going to be nervous, I’m going to be nervous. It’s going to be fun, a weird but cool experience, and yeah, I’m looking forward to it." Tkachuk totalled 213 goals and 250 assists for 463 points in 572 games with the Senators. He also guided them to back-to-back playoff appearances over the last two seasons. His relationship with the franchise seemed to crumble after he represented the U.S. at the 2026 Winter Olympics and defeated Canada in the gold-medal game.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources It didn’t take long for the top two picks of the 2026 NHL Entry Draft to meet on the ice. As the San Jose Sharks travelled to The Six to take on the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday, the focal point going into the game is the matchup between the first- and second-overall picks at the 2026 Draft: Gavin McKenna and Ivar Stenberg. It’s an often overblown narrative, as the stakes are as high as a blade of grass and sometimes neither rookie contributes in that game. But, hey: narratives are fun. This was the first time the two teams met in a truly competitive scenario. The played each other in a pre-tournament game before the 2026 World Juniors, but that’s really it. McKenna struggled that night, while Stenberg scored the game-winning goal. But now that both are established in the NHL, it’s going to be hard for them to avoid one another, even if they’re set to play in separate conferences for the foreseeable future. It’s fitting that this matchup came around the nine-game mark for both players, as that is a specific milestone for teenage rookies: it’s when their entry-level contracts can no longer slide. Cole Perfetti felt like an excellent option there, and Anton Lundell was easily the top two-way forward still available. Pittsburgh Penguins winger Bryan Rust suffered a lower-body injury during Pittsburgh’s 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth on Monday . The team confirmed that Rust would not return to the game following the injury. Rust, 34, did not come out for the third period, so it’s likely that the injury occured sometime during the second period. The exact cause or nature of the injury is unclear. The Pontiac, Michigan native put up two assists on Monday before leaving, giving him three goals and two assists for five points in seven games this season. He missed the first three games of the Penguins’ season with an upper-body injury he suffered late in the preseason. If Rust is forced to miss a significant amount of time, Pittsburgh will have to find someone to take his place on Crosby’s right wing. Last season, Rust notched 29 goals and 36 assists to tie his career best of 65 points in 72 games, before contributing a goal and an assist for two points during Pittsburgh’s first-round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Flyers in six games. Selected by the Penguins in the third round of the 2010 NHL Entry Draft, Rust debuted for the Penguins in the 2014-15 season after a four-year collegiate career with Notre Dame. items.body: Forward scores go-ahead goal against Sharks, wants 'to be a guy who is known for those big moments' TORONTO -- If Gavin McKenna has proven one thing so far in the infancy of his NHL career, it is that he does not shy away from big moments. In his first meeting against Ivar Stenberg , who was selected by the San Jose Sharks with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, McKenna, the No. 1 pick by the Toronto Maple Leafs, delivered the go-ahead goal and eventually game-winner, the first of his career, in a 3-1 victory at Scotiabank Arena on Monday. “I think it’s just a confidence thing,” McKenna said. “For me, you want to be a guy who is known for those big moments, so when you get the time and opportunity to be out there on the ice, you want to make the most out of it. When you are playing with guys like Auston (Matthews), Willy (Nylander) and those guys, I think it just brings confidence in itself. So for me, it’s something I take a lot of passion in, is trying to be known as a guy able to perform in those situations.” McKenna's goal came during a power play at 4:56 of the third period. Matthews recovered a rebound behind the net and sent a short pass to McKenna, who took the puck on his backhand before spinning toward the slot and shooting under the glove of Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov to give the Maple Leafs a 2-1 lead. “Pretty fired up,” he said. “I think it’s a hard league to score in, so when you get to put one in the back of the net, it feels pretty good.” Instead of immediately shooting, the 18-year-old showed patience. He used the time he realized he had and pulled the puck back, allowing Nylander to skate in front of him toward the near side of the net, which added another threat for Askarov to consider, before taking an extra step and shooting to the far side.

items.title: Mammoth hold off late charge to beat Penguins
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt and Nick Schmaltz all tallied a goal and an assist to help the Utah Mammoth beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-4 on Monday night. Kailer Yamamoto added a goal, and Sebastian Cossa had 15 stops for Utah. Erik Karlsson, Richard Rakell, Egor Chinakhov, and Declan Carlile each scored for Pittsburgh. Bryan Rust assisted on two goals. Arturs Silovs tallied 24 saves. Karlsson’s deflected power-play goal put the Penguins on the board just 71 seconds into the game. Keller levelled the score with a backhand at 6:00 of the first with his third goal in three games. Lawson Crouse snagged the puck near the boards and redirected it around Karlsson’s leg to Keller between the circles. Stenlund tapped in the puck from close range with 9:50 left in the first to give the Mammoth their first lead. Rakell tied it up on another power play goal at 7:01 of the second, flicking in a wrist shot near the left post. Utah surged back in front with a pair of goals late in the second. Schmidt reclaimed the lead with 8:16 to go, blasting a slapshot home from near the blue line. Yamamoto tipped in the puck from the low slot with 5:20 left to extend the lead. Schmaltz’s power play goal made it 5-2 for Utah at 1:36 of the third. Silovs denied his initial shot, but Schmaltz threaded a backhand around the goalie’s left leg on second effort. The Penguins cut the deficit to one late in the third period with goals from Chinakhov and Carlile. Chinakhov found the back of the net at 2:55 of the third. Carlile followed with a score off a wrist shot with 5:05 left.

items.summary: NEW YORK -- Nikita Kucherov and Vladislav Namestnikov stayed on the ice after the rest of the Tampa Bay Lightning players got kicked off.
items.body: Forward's detailed approach, mind for the game has led to success, 'he wasn't expected to be who he is' NEW YORK -- Nikita Kucherov and Vladislav Namestnikov stayed on the ice after the rest of the Tampa Bay Lightning players got kicked off. "Somehow they were able to weasel their way to stay on," former Lightning forward Tyler Johnson recalled. This was in 2013, during Kucherov's first NHL training camp. Johnson and Ondrej Palat were on the other side of the glass watching Kucherov and Namestnikov doing drills. "You could just see how detailed he was in everything he did," Johnson said. "He was thinking about the smallest of things: how he's stickhandling, where he's putting the puck, how he's protecting it. items.body: NEW YORK — Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, Dylan Garand made 29 saves and the New York Rangers defeated the travel-weary Anaheim Ducks 5-2 on Monday night to improve to 6-0-0 at home this fall. The Rangers did not pick up their sixth victory at Madison Square Garden last season until Jan. 26, their 23rd game there. They lost 27 of 41 at home on the way to missing the playoffs and finishing last in the Eastern Conference. There is hope of a turnaround given this start, even missing franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin for the rest of the season. Garand was making a fifth consecutive start since Shesterkin went down, and he has allowed two or fewer goals in nine of 10 NHL appearances dating to his debut last spring. He got support early and often, with Durzi's goal making it three home games in a row where the Rangers have a goal in the first two minutes. That has only happened once before for New York, in March 1989. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice, captain J.T. Miller and Gabe Perreault each had a goal and Alexis Lafrenière recorded two assists. Pavel Dorofeyev, the team's most notable trade acquisition over the summer, came close on several occasions but remained stuck on two goals for the season. Putting goalie Ville Husso in a tough spot with sloppy play, the Ducks looked every bit like a group that endured a 15-hour, delay-filled travel ordeal to the East Coast from southern California. They did not arrive at their hotel until 2:30 a.m., were on the ice for their morning skate less than nine hours later and were getting shut out until scoring twice in the final 70 seconds. items.body: Register Login Hurricanes Place Taylor Hall On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 19, 2026 7:30 pm The Hurricanes made a move to open up a roster spot on Monday, announcing that they’ve placed winger Taylor Hall on injured reserve. No immediate corresponding recall was made, leaving Carolina’s active roster at 22 players for the time being; they’re next in action on Tuesday. The 34-year-old sustained an upper-body injury last Tuesday against Washington. While there’s no firm timeline for his return, head coach Rod Brind’Amour recently noted that Hall is expected to be out week-to-week. Accordingly, it was only a matter of time before he landed on IR. Hall’s injury derailed what had been a strong start to his season. After finding another gear offensively in the playoffs when he had 19 points in as many games, he picked up three goals and two assists in eight games in the early going to this campaign. That had him on an early pace to surpass the 50-point mark for only the second time this decade but that will be considerably more challenging now given that he’ll miss at least a few weeks of action. Carolina’s recent injuries have allowed them to give looks to youngsters Bradly Nadeau and Felix Under Sorum. In the short term, it’s likely that they’ll continue to get some chances but with Hall’s placement, they now have the ability to recall someone else from AHL Chicago in the near future. With Mark Jankowski being evaluated for an injury sustained on Saturday against Winnipeg, that recall could be coming soon as they’re down to just 12 healthy forwards on their active roster.

Sean Higgins is facing two counts of first-degree aggravated manslaughter, two counts of second-degree reckless vehicular homicide, and one count each of tampering with physical evidence and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. Jury selection in Salem County, N.J., will begin on Dec. 1 and the trial will begin on Jan. 4 after a holiday break, according to The Athletic and ABC Action News 6 in Philadelphia. Higgins, 45, appeared in court on Monday and rejected a plea agreement. He faces up to 91 1/2 years in prison if found guilty of all charges, Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio said in court on Monday, according to The Athletic . Johnny Gaudreau, who played 11 seasons in the NHL with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets , and his brother Matthew Gaudreau died on Aug. 29, 2024, after they were struck by a car while riding their bikes near their family's home in rural New Jersey. Johnny was 31 and Matthew was 29.

items.title: Cole Knuble, son of Mike Knuble, makes NHL debut with Flyers
items.summary: On Monday night, he made his NHL debut for the team he grew up rooting for, with his parents in attendance.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Cole Knuble has fond memories of the Philadelphia Flyers ' home arena from his father, Mike, playing for them during his lengthy career. On Monday night, he made his NHL debut for the team he grew up rooting for, with his parents in attendance. The 22-year-old was one of three players called up from Lehigh Valley of the American Hockey League to fill in for injured forwards Owen Tippett, Tyson Foerster and Travis Konecny against Colorado. “Obviously I have been a fan of this team my whole life, so I think it’s extra special,” Knuble said. A fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft, Knuble nearly made the team out of training camp. He was disappointed to get sent to the minors but quickly adjusted his thinking. “I came (to camp) trying to make the team,” Knuble said. “But I think once I got down to Lehigh, the staff was so great. The players were all very welcoming, and I got to play in every situation. If you’re doing that, you can’t really complain too much, and I get an opportunity every game to kind of showcase myself and it’s a lot of fun.” Mike Knuble played 362 games, counting playoffs, with Philadelphia from 2005-09 and 2013.

items.summary: There’s a chance Connor Hellebuyck could suit up for the Winnipeg Jets in the near future.

items.body: Explanation : The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review confirmed that the actions of Colorado’s Josh Manson caused Philadelphia’s Porter Martone to contact Mackenzie Blackwood prior to Matvei Michkov’s goal . The decision was made in accordance with Note 2 of Rule 38.11 (ii) which states, in part, that the goal should be allowed because “the attacking Player was pushed, shoved or fouled by the defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper.” Penalty : 2:00 minor penalty: Delay of Game – Unsuccessful Challenge

items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs ' hot-handed winger will be available for Monday night's showdown against the San Jose Sharks (Sportsnet+, 7:30 p.m. ET / 10:30 p.m. PT) after previously being deemed a game-time decision due to an illness. Nylander missed the team's morning skate on Monday, with head coach Jim Hiller confirming that his status would be determined closer to game time. He took part in the team's warm-up before puck drop. The winger had been slated to skate on the top line alongside Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic, but Bo Groulx skated as a placeholder for Nylander at Monday's practice. Before going two games without a point heading into Monday's clash, Nylander had been on a hot streak to start the season, tallying five goals and seven assists in the team's first seven games. The Maple Leafs are in the midst of a three-game skid, losing to the Utah Mammoth, Buffalo Sabres and New York Islanders, and have dropped to last place in the Atlantic.

items.title: ‘We’ve got a long ways to go’: Rebuilding Canucks aim to snap losing skid
items.summary: Vancouver has struggled to keep pace with its opponents.
items.body: Luke Schenn believes his Vancouver Canucks need to be "a heck of a lot better." The veteran defenceman's comments come after the NHL team sputtered through an early-season Eastern Conference road swing, going 0-5-1 and getting outscored 27-11. "Obviously, you come back pretty humble, to say the least," Schenn said Monday. "And we've got a long ways to go, for sure." The winless trip extended Vancouver's losing skid to seven games. Outside expectations for the rebuilding Canucks were low heading into the 2026-27 campaign. The squad stunned many in a season-opening 6-5 overtime victory over the Oilers, and continued to raise eyebrows in a 9-7 loss to Edmonton two nights later. But after beating the Calgary Flames 4-1 on home ice back on Oct. 3, Vancouver has struggled to keep pace with its opponents. "I totally understand it's about the process and getting better over time," Schenn said. items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Cole Schwindt; Reassign Sam Lafferty By Brennan McClain | at October 19, 2026 6:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Florida Panthers recalled forward Cole Schwindt from the AHL’s Charlotte Checkers. In a corresponding roster move, the Panthers assigned forward Sam Lafferty the other way. Schwindt, 25, recently played his first AHL contests since the 2023-24 season, then with the Calgary Flames. Since the Panthers entered the 2026-27 campaign relatively healthy, Schwindt didn’t make Florida’s opening-night roster. He has performed relatively well with the Checkers, scoring one goal and three points in five games with a -1 rating. Still, Schwindt earned an extended stay with the Panthers last season because the team dealt with so many injuries. He was on that list early in the season, fracturing his arm in November, which caused him to miss several months. He finished the campaign with five goals and seven points in 29 games with a +2 rating, averaging 10:02 of ice time per game. Meanwhile, Lafferty is headed to AHL Charlotte to delay his waiver eligibility. The eight-year NHL veteran was recalled on October 3rd after captain Aleksander Barkov was injured. On the roster since then, Lafferty was only five games and/or 14 days from requiring waivers for reassignment again. Furthermore, Lafferty didn’t start great. Joining the Panthers this past offseason on a one-year, $850K contract, Lafferty went scoreless in five games with a -4 rating. Even though he began over 70% of his shifts in the offensive zone, Lafferty won only eight of his 32 draws. He also owns the worst CorsiFor on the team at 36.4% in all situations.

items.summary: The Winnipeg Jets are officially on the clock for a deadline they would much rather ignore.

When Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman broke the news minutes before Saturday's puck drop, the ripple effect through the organization was swift.
